title: Anthropic raises $107.3bn in the biggest IPO ever
excerpt: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share, above its range, raising $107.3bn with a private placement in the largest IPO on record.
content_html:
Anthropic priced its initial public offering at $83 a share on Wednesday, above its marketed range of $70 to $78. The company and its seven co-founders raised a record $107.3bn from the IPO and a private placement, Bloomberg reported.

The shares are due to start trading on Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker ANT.

Anthropic upsized the offering and sold about 980 million shares, CNBC reported, citing a company press release. That share sale alone raised $81.3bn. Seven companies, including Google, Nvidia and Microsoft, also agreed to buy $26bn of stock in a private placement at the IPO price.

Bloomberg counts the two together. Either way, the deal is the largest IPO on record, ahead of SpaceX’s listing in June.

Anthropic first offered 825 million shares at the start of its roadshow on 10 November, according to a company statement. Demand was strong. Institutional investors placed orders worth about $400bn ahead of pricing, CNBC reported earlier, citing people familiar with the deal.

The price is about 41% above what investors paid in Anthropic’s private round in May, which valued the company at $965bn. At $83, the company is worth about $1.5tn on a fully diluted basis.

Bloomberg said the deal makes Anthropic the first frontier AI lab to raise money on public markets. The listing comes as investors have grown more cautious about AI stocks.

The company’s rival OpenAI has also said it plans to go public.
